Published online:
    September 3, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: US, Japan, Europe, Middle East)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Global risk assets rallied ahead of Friday's US payrolls report, with bonds recovering from multi-year yield highs, the yen surging, and the dollar weakening. Fed rate hike probability for the current month jumped to ~60% from sub-40% a week prior. Fed speakers (Williams, Waller) are in focus. Geopolitical risk from US-Iran military exchanges is pressuring oil and supporting gold, which is near record highs. Dutch central bank gold repatriation adds a subtle de-dollarization signal.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — The article directly covers US 10-year yields (4.766%), Fed rate hike expectations, payrolls data, Fed Governor commentary, and broad US asset pricing implications.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (85 on a scale of 0 [NO] to 100 [YES])
Probability of increase: 60% (explicitly stated by money markets for the current month)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 25 (25 on a scale of 0 [NO] to 100 [YES])
Probability of holding: 40% (implied residual from the 60% hike probability; Williams noted he is still "collecting information," leaving door open)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (5 on a scale of 0 [NO] to 100 [YES])
Probability of decrease: 0% (no cut narrative present; trajectory is firmly tightening-biased)

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 65 (65 on a scale of -100 [More dovish than before] to 100 [More hawkish than before]) — Rate hike odds jumped sharply from <40% to ~60% in one week, Williams framed higher yields as a sign of economic strength rather than stress, and Friday payrolls data is expected to further cement the hawkish case. The tone is meaningfully more hawkish than prior positioning, though residual uncertainty ahead of payrolls caps the reading short of maximum hawkishness.
